IRAN WAR UPDATE — MAY 5, 2026

The ceasefire is still alive…

But barely.

The Strait of Hormuz crisis has reignited — and this time, the fire is spreading from the waterway to the wider Gulf.

🔸 It began with Trump’s “Project Freedom” — a US naval plan to help trapped commercial ships move through the Strait of Hormuz.

Washington framed it as a mission to reopen global trade.

Tehran saw it as a direct challenge.

Iran warned that any foreign military force trying to enter the strait would face a “decisive and crushing response”.

Then the shooting started.

🔸 US Central Command says Iranian forces fired cruise missiles, drones and fast boats at US warships and commercial vessels.

The US says it destroyed several Iranian small boats and successfully helped US-flagged commercial ships pass through the strait.

Iran denies this version.

Tehran says the boats hit by the US were civilian vessels carrying goods and passengers — and that five civilians were killed.

Two completely different stories.

One extremely dangerous waterway.

🔸 Then came the shock: the UAE was hit.

The UAE says it intercepted ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones launched from Iran.

A drone attack sparked a fire at Fujairah — one of the UAE’s most important oil hubs.

Three Indian nationals were injured.

This matters because Fujairah is not just another port.

It is the UAE’s oil escape hatch — built outside the Strait of Hormuz so Abu Dhabi can keep exporting crude even when the strait is paralysed.

In simple terms:

Iran may not just be threatening the main oil route.

It may also be threatening the backup route.

🔸 Iran has not officially claimed the UAE attack.

Instead, an Iranian military official blamed “US adventurism”, saying Tehran had no pre-planned intention to strike UAE oil facilities.

But the UAE is not buying it.

Abu Dhabi called the attack “treacherous” and said it reserves the right to respond.

Gulf states, the GCC, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Jordan, India, Pakistan, Canada, France, Germany, the UK and the EU all condemned the attack or backed the UAE.

The message from the region is clear:

No one wants the Gulf dragged back into full war.

But everyone can feel it getting closer.

🔸 Trump responded with one of his strongest threats yet.

He warned Iran would be “blown off the face of the earth” if US Navy ships are attacked in Hormuz.

At the same time, he appears reluctant to fully restart the war.

That is the dangerous contradiction now:

Washington wants to force Hormuz open.

Iran wants to prove it still controls the chokepoint.

And both sides are trying not to look like the one that killed the ceasefire.

🔸 South Korea has now been pulled into the story.

A South Korean-operated vessel suffered an explosion and fire near the strait.

Trump urged Seoul to join Project Freedom.

South Korea is reviewing the request carefully, saying it must consider international law.

This is how a regional war becomes a global shipping crisis.

One ship at a time.

🔸 Israel and Hezbollah are also exchanging fire again in southern Lebanon.

Israel issued new evacuation orders for Lebanese towns.

Hezbollah says it targeted Israeli soldiers, vehicles, tanks and bulldozers.

An Israeli drone strike in Gaza City also killed one Palestinian and injured others.

So while the headlines focus on Hormuz, the wider war map is still active.

Gaza.
Lebanon.
The Gulf.
The UAE.
The Strait.

Everything is connected.

🔸 Markets finally reacted.

Brent crude surged almost 6% to around $114–115 a barrel.

US crude closed above $106.

European shares fell.

The FTSE 100 dropped around 1%.

Wall Street slipped from record highs.

The Dow fell more than 550 points.

The 30-year US Treasury yield pushed above 5% as investors worried higher oil means higher inflation for longer.

This is the market’s fear:

Not just war.

Inflation returning through the oil pump.

🔸 That fear is already spreading.

US analysts warn petrol could hit $5 per gallon by June even if a Hormuz deal is reached soon.

Australia raised interest rates again, blaming higher fuel and commodity prices.

The Philippines and Pakistan are seeing inflation jump.

Thailand approved a $12.2 billion emergency borrowing package to cushion the economic shock.

Iran is also under heavy pressure.

Inflation is around 50%.

Food prices are surging.

Tehran is rolling out electronic vouchers for around 87 million people and threatening harsh punishment for price gouging.

This is no longer just a military war.

It is an energy war.
A shipping war.
A currency war.
A household-cost war.

🔸 Meanwhile, diplomacy is still alive — but fragile.

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says there is “no military solution to a political crisis”.

Pakistan is trying to mediate.

Saudi Arabia is urging restraint.

Europe is calling for Hormuz to reopen.

But on the water, missiles, drones and warships are doing the talking.

Final takeaway:

Hormuz is no longer just a narrow sea lane.

It is becoming the pressure valve of the global economy.

When it closes, oil rises.

When oil rises, inflation rises.

When inflation rises, central banks panic.

When central banks panic, markets shake.

And when markets shake, every household eventually feels it.

The ceasefire still technically exists.

But today, it looks less like peace…

and more like a matchstick floating on petrol.

#IranWar #OilPrices #Hormuz

LEVISTE VS. RECTO: TENSYON SA PLENARYO

Uminit ang sesyon sa House of Representatives of the Philippines matapos ang  banggaan sa pagitan nina Cong. Leandro Legarda Leviste at ni Ryan, anak ni Ralph Recto nitong Martes, May 5.

Sa kanyang privilege speech, diretsahang inihain ni Leviste ang panawagan para sa imbestigasyon kaugnay ng umano’y koneksyon ni Ralph Recto kay Edwin Gardiola, na iniuugnay sa isyu ng flood control projects.

MATITINDING BANAT SA PLENARYO

Sa bahagi ng kanyang talumpati, hindi nagpatumpik-tumpik si Leviste sa pagsagot sa umano’y pagtawag sa kanya na “baliw” ni Ralph Recto:

“Kung baliw man ako, at least hindi ako magnanakaw.”

Ipinahiwatig din niya na ang mga umano’y pag-atake laban sa kanya ay nagsimula matapos niyang imbestigahan ang mga proyekto:

“Nagsimula lang itong mga atake sa akin nang sinimulan kong imbestigahan ang DPWH sa Batangas at ang mga kumpanyang konektado kay Congressman Edwin Gardiola…”

BAGONG AKUSASYON: ₱1 BILYONG GASTOS?

Bukod sa koneksyon sa flood control issue, naglatag din si Leviste ng mabigat na alegasyon kaugnay ng umano’y malaking halaga ng perang ginamit sa pulitika:

“Ayon sa aking tantya at pananaliksik, mahigit one billion pesos ang ginastos ni Congressman Edwin Gardiola para kina Vilma Santos-Recto at Lucky Manzano, at sa iba pa nilang mga kandidato…”

Dagdag pa niya, ito umano ang isa lamang sa mga puntong nais niyang ilahad, at may iba pa siyang ibubunyag sa mga susunod na araw.

PANAWAGAN NG IMBESTIGASYON

Giit ni Leviste, bahagi ng kanyang tungkulin bilang mambabatas ang pagbubunyag ng umano’y iregularidad:

“Hindi ito para sa sarili ko… ito ay bahagi ng aking tungkulin bilang mambabatas… kaya ako nananawagan na imbestigahan ang koneksyon ni Gardiola kay Recto…”

Idinagdag din niya ang panawagan na suriin ang posibleng papel ng Malacañang:

“…at suriin ni Pangulong Bongbong Marcos kung may natutulungan si Recto mula sa loob ng Malacañang.”

DEPENSA NG KAMPO NI RECTO

Samantala, sa panig ni Ralph Recto, nagsalita ang kanyang anak na si Rep. Ryan Recto, at pinabulaanan ang mga alegasyon at iginiit na walang basehan ang mga paratang.

Ang banggaan ay bahagi ng lumalawak na bangayan sa pagitan ng dalawang kampo—na nagsimula sa social media at ngayo’y umabot na sa mismong plenaryo ng Kongreso.

Bukod sa flood control controversy, nadawit na rin sa diskurso ang mas malalim na usapin ng transparency, accountability, at umano’y impluwensya ng ehekutibo sa lehislatura.

Sa ngayon, nananatiling alegasyon ang mga pahayag at hinihintay pa kung magkakaroon ng pormal na imbestigasyon o karagdagang ebidensya sa mga susunod na araw.

PANAWAGAN NG IMBESTIGASYON Giit ni Leviste, bahagi ng kanyang tungkulin bilang mambabatas ang pagbubunyag ng umano’y iregularidad: “Hindi ito para sa sarili ko… ito ay bahagi ng aking tungkulin bilang mambabatas… kaya ako nananawagan na imbestigahan ang koneksyon ni Gardiola kay Recto…” Idinagdag din niya ang panawagan na suriin ang posibleng papel ng Malacañang: “…at suriin ni Pangulong Bongbong Marcos kung may natutulungan si Recto mula sa loob ng Malacañang.” DEPENSA NG KAMPO NI RECTO Samantala, sa panig ni Ralph Recto, nagsalita ang kanyang anak na si Rep. Ryan Recto, at pinabulaanan ang mga alegasyon at iginiit na walang basehan ang mga paratang. Ang banggaan ay bahagi ng lumalawak na bangayan sa pagitan ng dalawang kampo—na nagsimula sa social media at ngayo’y umabot na sa mismong plenaryo ng Kongreso. Bukod sa flood control controversy, nadawit na rin sa diskurso ang mas malalim na usapin ng transparency, accountability, at umano’y impluwensya ng ehekutibo sa lehislatura. Sa ngayon, nananatiling alegasyon ang mga pahayag at hinihintay pa kung magkakaroon ng pormal na imbestigasyon o karagdagang ebidensya sa mga susunod na araw.
